Zoe Park: FYI - emergency assist for customer 'Pioneer Labs' private deploy. They lost access to their keystore during an oncall failover and we did an emergency RBAC grant to restore decrypts. Raising a flag: audit events for that grant didn't show up in SIEM for ~40m.
Anil Rao: timeline? what was changed during failover?
Zoe Park: at 2026-03-05T14:00 UTC ops triggered failover; at 14:03 we performed `kmsctl grant --key key-pli-20260305 --principal svc-pioneer-ks --actions decrypt` to restore service. App recover confirmed at 14:05.
sec-bot: Detected: RBAC_CHANGE event at 2026-03-05T14:03:12Z (actor=oncall@infra), audit-id=rbac-20260305-14.
Clara D'Souza: SIEM shows rotation and failover events, but the RBAC_CHANGE entry missing until 14:45. Any netpol changes during that window?
Oncall Ops: we tightened egress for the audit-forwarder in that maintenance window as part of isolation hardening (deny-by-default + explicit whitelist). Netflow shows audit-forwarder couldn't reach siem-collector IPs 14:02-14:42.
Anil Rao: so audit was generated locally but blocked from egress. Where were the local logs stored?
Oncall Ops: audit logs persisted to /var/log/keystore/audit.log and a separate file for infra-agent at /var/log/infra/rotations.log. We shipped them at 14:42 after we temporarily reopened egress and forwarded backlog.
Zoe Park: customer compliance is asking for a signed attestation that the grant only lasted X minutes and that we didn't widen permissions. We need to provide proof chain: who granted, justification, and exact duration.
sec-bot: Retrieved local audit snippet (sanitized): `2026-03-05T14:03:12Z audit RBAC_CHANGE key=key-pli-20260305 principal=svc-pioneer-ks actor=oncall@infra reason="emergency failover" duration_hint=temporary`. Also infra-agent rotation log shows `failover-mode=true` at 14:01.
Clara D'Souza: mitigation checklist: 1) ensure audit-forwarder egress exceptions are always enabled for SIEM IPs during maintenance, 2) add a fail-safe that writes signed audit entries to immutable storage (S3-like) before any RBAC emergency grant completes, 3) add a policy that emergency grants create a mandatory ephemeral token with TTL and auto-revoke job, 4) add alert when audit-forwarder backlog > 0 for >5m.
Anil Rao: security follow-up: we should rotate the emergency-granted key material after confirming no misuse window. Also run a quick vuln triage: could an attacker exploit temporary egress rules to intercept logs or perform a malicious key swap?
Oncall Ops: confirm we replayed the backlog to SIEM; we captured the exact grant command in local audit and the manual revoke at 15:10 recorded via `kmsctl revoke --key key-pli-20260305 --principal svc-pioneer-ks`.
Zoe Park: actions I'm taking: - prepare signed attestation bundle for customer (include local audit snippet + SIEM ingest timestamp + manual revoke entry), - open INF-8001 to add immutable pre-commit for emergency grants, - open INF-8002 to add audit-forwarder egress whitelist guard during maintenance, - INF-8003 to implement auto-revoke TTL for emergency grants.
Clara D'Souza: add a detection rule: if any RBAC_CHANGE has no corresponding SIEM ingest within 10 minutes, page oncall and automatically re-open audit-forwarder egress for 30m.
sec-bot: Note: added incident tags RBAC-EGRESS-20260305 and queued artifacts: local audit log snippet, rotation log, netflow capture, SIEM ingest confirmation (14:44).
Anil Rao: one more compliance ask: confirm that keystore-proxy rejected any decrypts outside the window. Oncall Ops, can you produce decrypt access logs showing only normal calls from 14:05-15:10 and that no elevated operations occurred?
Oncall Ops: yes will export decrypt access log with timestamps and include a hash-signed bundle. Upload ETA 2 hours.
Zoe Park: thanks. We'll circulate the attestation to Pioneer Labs and include the remediation plan and timeline. I'll post the postmortem in #eng-security once artifacts are bundled. :thumbsup:
